- Acrylic paint (recommended for most beginners and hobby canvas work)
  - Pros: water‑soluble, non‑toxic, quick drying, easy cleanup, versatile (can be thinned or thickened), many finishes.
  - Use: pre‑primed or gesso‑primed canvas works well. Good for layering and mixed‑media.
- Oil paint
  - Pros: rich colors, long open working time for blending, durable finish.
  - Cons: slow drying, needs solvents/odor control, more setup/ventilation.
  - Use: also on primed canvas; best if you want traditional fine‑art techniques and time to blend.
- Watercolor / gouache
  - Generally not ideal directly on standard canvas (they’re for paper). You can use them on specially prepared/primed canvas, but acrylics are simpler.
- Other notes
  - Prime your canvas with gesso if it’s unprimed.
  - Consider paint bodies: heavy‑body acrylic for texture, fluid acrylics for washes.
  - Finish with an appropriate varnish (gloss/matte) after drying.
  - If you want low‑odor or quick results, pick acrylic; for slow blending and classic look, pick oils.
